Consult Summary:
- 35-year-old male with 4-day history of sore throat, runny nose, evolving cough, myalgia, headache, night sweats, and initial fever; likely viral upper respiratory tract infection.

History:
- Presenting complaint: 4 days of feeling unwell, started with sore throat and runny nose; sore throat improving, now with new dry cough and persistent nasal congestion. 
- Associated symptoms: Fatigue, night sweats, headaches (intermittent, generalized), muscle aches (onset in past 2 days), feeling winded on exertion, decreased appetite, increased thirst. 
- Negative findings: No chest pain, no dyspnea at rest, no ear pain or discharge, no visual changes, no photophobia, no nausea or vomiting, normal bowel and urinary habits, no skin rash, no joint pain beyond muscle aches.
- Past medical history: No chronic illnesses; no regular medications except for Paracetamol and Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) used during current illness.
- Allergies: None reported.
- Family history: Grandmother with type 2 diabetes; great-grandfather with eczema.
- Social history: Lives alone; works as an accountant; occasional cigar smoking at social events; occasional alcohol use; currently still working but experiencing increased work-related stress (denies negative impact on mood); no significant psychosocial concerns discussed.
- Preventive care: Not mentioned.

Examination:
- No examination findings documented.
- No vitals documented.

Impression:
- Likely viral upper respiratory tract infection (URTI); possible early influenza.

Plan:
- Supportive care: Advise rest, increased fluid intake, and continued use of Paracetamol and Ibuprofen as needed.
- Recommend time off from work (1–2 days).
- Safety net advice: Return if symptoms worsen (fever persists, dyspnea, chest pain), or if not improved within one week.
- Follow-up: Return visit if no improvement after one week or sooner if deterioration.

Quality checks:

● Missing elements: Age, sex, allergies, and medication reconciliation were only partially covered; no physical examination or vitals performed/documented; immunization status and travel history not addressed.
● Internal conflicts: None noted.
● Transcript quality: Good; minimal irrelevant content. All clinically relevant history covered.
